text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: tenant=apexcore (TEN-APX-42) — model_latency_p95 > 1200ms for 6m, error_rate=8.3% > threshold. Paged oncall-sre.

Sara: saw the page, joining. summary pls?

Miguel: initial triage — dedicated pool eu-west-2 serving apexcore is showing token errors and timeouts on open-xl-13b-v2-fp16. Errors look like decoding failures + occasional OOMs at high seq len. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/TEN-APX-42/metrics (link)

Raj: I'm on logs. I can see spikes correlated with long prompt traffic between 1.2–1.6k tokens. KV cache growth + a handful of 500s from runtime.

Elena: network/team note — no infra-level network blips. GPUs healthy but memory pressure for some tasks. Could be a model/kernel codepath issue under long-seq.

Sara: customer impact — ApexCore reports increased error rate for their live chat -> visible to users (some automated messages failing). They are on a reserved/dedicated plan; this needs fast mitigation and clear comms.

Miguel: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) pin tenant to a previous safe model variant, 2) enable traffic split to route some traffic to a quantized fallback, 3) temporarily limit max_seq_len for this tenant. Thoughts?

Raj: agree. My preference: pin to v2-rc3? but v2 is where problems appear. safer: pin to v1-stable (open-xl-13b-v1-fp16) as primary and use v2 as canary OR pin to v2 but set fallback to v1. Which preserves ordering for them?

Elena: customer expects same behavior as earlier this week (they upgraded automatically). They asked for minimal behavioral drift — so pinning to v2 but routing some to v1 might still surface the bug. I'd rather pin to v1-stable for immediate user safety, then canary v2 later.

Sara: decision: pin tenant to open-xl-13b-v1-stable for immediate user safety, set fallback policy to v2 (canary) once we've validated. Notify account team.

Miguel: executing pin now. API call:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/TEN-APX-42/pin \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-xl-13b-v1-stable","reason":"mitigate production degradation","duration":"6h"}'
```

IncidentBot: COMMAND RECEIVED — pin request queued (req_id=pin-3193334444-7).

Miguel: API returned 200. pin active. Confirming routing table update...

IncidentBot: ROUTE_UPDATED — tenant=TEN-APX-42 routes: primary=open-xl-13b-v1-stable, fallback=open-xl-13b-v2-fp16 (canary 10%).

Raj: created temporary traffic-shaping rule to cap long-seq requests to 1024 tokens for that tenant to reduce kv cache pressure:

```
# tenant config
{"tenant":"TEN-APX-42","max_seq_len":1024}
```

Elena: pushed the max_seq_len cap. Watchers: applied to edge and runtime, may increase client error if they send longer prompts. Account notified first.

ApexCore-Customer-Notifier (via acct-team): FYI — we've asked their SRE to throttle client long messages while we stabilize.

Miguel: metrics update in 5m. so far p95 down from 1300ms -> ~420ms after pin, error_rate down to 1.1%. Looks promising.

Sara: good. next steps: 1) continue monitoring 15–30m, 2) run targeted evals on v2 to reproduce failures, 3) open internal bug with runtime + model-onboarding for v2 kernel path.

Raj: raising issue: https://issues.redwood.ai/INT-8071 (internal) with logs + stack traces. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

Elena: also scheduling a short canary: route 5% to v2 in 30m once we have more telemetry. If stable, ramp to 25%, then decide for full rollback/upgrade.

Miguel: adding temporary alert suppressions to avoid noise while actions in flight. will revert after resolution.

IncidentBot: NOTE — oncall handover set for +2h. next oncall: @oncall-pager.

Sara: leaving handoff notes: pinned tenant to v1-stable, set max_seq_len cap=1024, created fallback/canary pair, notified account. Observed p95 improvements and error reduction. Postmortem owner needed.

Elena: assigning postmortem owner — miguel. can you own?

Miguel: I can. Will coordinate with eng-runtime and eng-ml. Scheduling postmortem doc and RFC for safer rollout checks.

Raj: small follow-up action — add per-tenant pre-check that runs synthetic long-seq eval on model variants before automatic upgrades. I’ll draft the checklist.

ApexCore-Account (acct-team): customer acknowledges mitigation, asks for ETA to return to v2. We'll ask for 24–48h to validate.

Sara: agreed. communicate a conservative ETA and keep them in the loop.

Miguel: logging final state: pinned->open-xl-13b-v1-stable, fallback->open-xl-13b-v2-fp16 (canary 5%), max_seq_len=1024, suppress-alerts TTL=2h.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=customer-impact, status=mitigated, owner=miguel. Postmortem requested.

oncall-pager: acknowledged. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if regressions appear.

Sara: thanks all. leaving this thread for follow-ups in postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

Miguel: uploading debug bundle and runbook notes to the incident doc now.

Raj: drafting the pre-upgrade synthetic checks PR — will link when ready.

Elena: adding config to tenant-policy repo to prevent automatic model promotion until health checks pass.

Sara: closing thread for live mitigation. we will reopen if new alerts spike.
